text.p: An offering of shares in chemicals group Kemira Oy may come this autumn, a senior official at Finland's ministry of trade and industry said on Friday.
In an interview with Reuters, permanent under-secretary of state Matti Vuoria said the government would soon look at fresh ways to broaden Kemira's ownership.
"It would appropriate for the government to look at it in the near future since studies have been made," he said, adding action was possible this autumn.
"I would consider it possible," he said.
The ministry last spring mandated Goldman Sachs as advisor on Kemira's ownership. The state currently owns 72.3 percent of Kemira and has an authorisation to lower this to 50.1 percent.
In general, stock market conditions were good for privatisation and the state's listed companies were structurally ready, Vuoria said.
"The outlook for broadening ownership in state companies is very favourable now," Vuoria said.
The government's last move was this summer's successful offering of some 22 million shares in Valmet Oy which raised some 2.4 billion markka.

"Outokumpu's and Rautaruukki's, structures are very clear, the same goes for Kemira. Enso too is similar, it has had a huge restructuring when Enso-Gutzeit and Veitsiluoto were merged, and (for Enso) we are just sort of waiting for the markets to develop," he said.
"For these large companies this is in a way more like business as usual, waiting for the right time," he added.
For oil and energy group Neste, an international offering was on the agenda, he said, but did not specify.
"We will also have to look at the chances to broaden its international ownership," he said.

Electricity producer Imatran Voima Oy has been expected to be partly privatised and listed on the Helsinki Stock Exchange next year and Vuoria said the final precondition -- divesting Imatran Voima's national grid into a new separate national grid company -- may be fulfilled at the turn of the year.
"After the national grid issue has been settled, we can start looking at IVO's ownership base," he said.

The government on Friday launched a programme to up its own research and development spending to 7.5 billion by 1999, 1.5 billion markka more than earlier plans, which it said was possible without widening the budget gap due to the favourable privatisation outlook.

The government can execute this programme and in addition cover one billion markka per year of its deficit with its current privatisation mandate from parliament, Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki told a news conference.

The government has authorisation to lower its stake in steel group Rautaruukki to 33.4 percent from 68.7 percent, in forestry group Enso to 33.4 percent from 44.5 percent, in Valmet to nil from 20 percent and in Neste to 50.1 percent from 84 percent.
The smallest room to manoeuvre is in Outokumpu where it has authorisation to lower the stake to just 33.4 percent of shares from 39.97 percent currently.
